objective: Fix owner-visible manual model warmup failures, make bounded Cloud vision analysis return a complete usable overview instead of falsely rejecting a punctuation-complete budget-bound answer, expose truthful desktop capture/analysis timing, and apply the owner's approved 15.5 GiB Hina GPU budget without double-reserving Windows' already-measured GPU use.
non_goals: Do not add a model, dependency, background capture, automatic screen observation, image persistence, or remote control surface.
Do not ignore NVIDIA live-free telemetry, overcommit physical VRAM, force Cloud vision into local VRAM, or enable CPU fallback for the GPU desktop profile.
Do not run repeat, soak, full-release, or deep VRAM benchmark workflows unless the owner explicitly requests them.
contracts: The 15.5 GiB (15,872 MiB) Hina admission ceiling is capped by live NVIDIA free VRAM; Windows/other-process usage is already represented by that live value and is not subtracted a second time.
Manual brain/STT warmup uses only the existing shared GPU scheduler and pin/unload lifecycle; an owner action never silently falls back to CPU or bypasses admission.
A model warmup may use a separate bounded warmup deadline, never the short health probe deadline used for availability checks.

Vision performs no more than two Cloud/local requests per snapshot. A final answer at an output-token boundary is accepted only when it passes bounded completeness checks; otherwise recovery requests a shorter complete overview and still fails closed on incomplete content.
Desktop capture progress/timings expose only phase durations and capture dimensions/bytes, never source IDs, raw pixels, API keys, hidden model text, or additional persistence.
allowed_dependencies: Existing Python standard library, current scheduler/provider interfaces, Electron typed IPC, and Vue/CSS; no new dependency.
acceptance_criteria: Force-load brain waits long enough for a real local Ollama cold load and reports a bounded provider error only after that deadline.
Force-load Systran/faster-whisper-large-v3 is supported through a GPU lease, remains resident until owner unload/preemption, and is never changed to CPU fallback.
Resource page reports a 15.5 GiB Hina ceiling and accurately explains that live-free VRAM remains the hard physical limit.
A budget-bound VLM final answer ending cleanly is accepted; incomplete first output receives at most one concise recovery request, and incomplete second output remains an explicit error.
The capture page changes from capture to analysis progress and shows bounded capture/runtime/total timing after completion without retaining pixels.
Focused unit/build/typecheck tests pass; one read-only NVIDIA/Ollama resource snapshot is recorded in docs rather than retaining raw test artifacts.
